Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement reviewed the MSA + order form and flagged a few items they need clarified before we can sign: specifically the auto-renew notice window, termination for convenience (TFC) rights and the service transfer / transition assistance obligations if either party exits.

Their asks (summary):
- 90-day written notice to opt-out of auto-renew (they want more lead time).
- Explicit mutual TFC with 90-day exit window and scope for transition assistance (knowledge transfer, data export, and a staffed handover for up to 45 days).
- Pro rata invoice treatment and confirmation on refund timing (we currently seen as 30 days in system).

I attached the procurement RFI and marked the relevant sections. Can your legal team propose redlines that address the above? Also need a clear statement of any extra fees if Redwood provides extended transition services beyond standard support.

We’re hoping to get a final answer by COB Monday (22nd) to keep our internal procurement timeline intact.

Thanks,

Hi Alyssa — Laura Bennett from Legal here. Thanks for the clear summary. Based on Redwood’s standard positions and to preserve operational stability across customers, our suggested starting redlines are below (attached as Doc): Redline_MSA_Acme_v3.docx.

Summary of proposed language (high level):
- Auto-renew: Order Form will auto-renew for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives written notice to non-renew at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term.
- Termination for Convenience (mutual): Either party may terminate for convenience with 60 days’ prior written notice. Upon such termination Redwood will provide transition assistance as set out in an attached SOW.
- Transition assistance: Standard transition assistance included for up to 30 days (remote knowledge transfer, data export, transfer of runbooks). Extended on‑site or staffed handover to be billable per the SOW rates; cap to be negotiated.
- Refunds/invoicing: Fees for the remainder of the then-current invoiced month are pro rata and refundable within 30 days of final reconciliation.

Rationale: 60 days is our baseline to balance procurement needs with the operational burden of model handovers and capacity planning. If Acme requires 90 days and/or 45 days of staffed transition, that’s possible but will require an explicit SOW and a one-time transition fee to cover dedicated engineering time.

I attached the redline and a draft Service-Transfer-SOW that defines the scope and pricing bands for extended assistance. Please review and let us know which items are deal-breakers; I can iterate quickly.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redline_MSA_Acme_v3.docx (docx)]

Hi Alyssa — Priyom here (Solutions/Sales Ops). Appreciate the procurement context. To propose a pragmatic compromise:

- Notice window: 75 days for non-renew and TFC (splits the difference between 60 / 90).
- Transition assistance: 30 days staffed transition included in the SOW; if Acme requires up to 45 days staffed, we can provide that as an add-on at a fixed, capped rate (we suggest a daily rate with an overall cap equal to 25% of the then-current monthly contract value).
- Auto-renew opt-out lead time (aligned): 75 days prior to term end.
- Refunds: pro rata refunds reconciled and paid within 30 days; outstanding invoices netted.

If that framework is acceptable, Laura can prepare the updated redline and SOW language (we’ll add explicit language about capped staffed days and pricing). From a scheduling perspective, we can get an updated order form to you by Wednesday if we get sign-off on the compromise by end of day tomorrow.

Karthik — happy to coordinate any commercial concessions if we need C-suite approval for the transition fee cap.
